items.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021
items.q: And it was called Gino’s Empty Foxhole after the guy who was putting together the shows, Gino.

ctx.x: He turned lights on before I ever met him. When I was in college I had taken a trip to a college in another city to — and I met someone who played for me the album by Sun Ra “Nothing Is.” Okay? And that was my first exposure to Sun Ra, in a dorm room with someone playing the album “Nothing Is.” And it blew my mind. The first listen it blew

my mind. The poetry on the cover, the poetry on the back cover, I mean that — I can’t say it resonated with me I would have to say it blew my mind, the music and the whole presentation. And then it just so happens that when I returned to Philadelphia, you know Sun Ra was living there and I would have opportunities to see him. Crazy. And I saw him which remains to this day the — probably the greatest concert of my life. And it still today binds a lot of people, this concert and this scene. There was a place on…
If someone came into your store and said, “Well I took a chance and I bought a Sun Ra LP and I just don’t get it. I don’t understand it” —
